calls.title: Hampus / Luke
calls.summary: The discussion centered on Growth Book's two experimentation engines: the frequentist engine, which applies multiple comparison corrections using methods like Holm-Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg only for gold metrics, and a Bayesian engine that currently does not utilize these corrections. Luke Sonnet and Hampus explored opportunities for improving data analytics, including conducting meta-analyses using stored customer experiment snapshots. They highlighted the significance of granular data and discussed the operational challenges customers face with feature flags, noting the necessity of cleaning up stale experiments. Future initiatives include setting up hands-on demos and better documentation for customer education, while also considering how to build a more complex Bayesian model informed by historical customer data.
calls.keywords: Multiple Hypothesis Correction, Bayesian Engine, Frequentist Engine, SEO Content Strategy, Experiment Snapshots, Feature Flags
